b1: Adrenaline/noradrenaline here speeds the heart and makes it squeeze harder.
b2: Activation relaxes airway muscle, opening the airways.
a1: Activation squeezes blood vessels, raising blood pressure.
a2: Activation turns DOWN sympathetic output from the brain.
m: Acetylcholine here slows the heart, makes saliva, constricts the pupil.
nm: Acetylcholine opens this channel to make skeletal muscle contract.
ache: Chops up acetylcholine to end its signal.
mu: Pain pathways in brain and spinal cord
Natural endorphins here reduce pain signals.
d2: Dopamine signalling for movement, motivation and thinking.
ht3: Serotonin here triggers nausea and vomiting.
ht1: Activation narrows dilated head vessels and calms pain nerves.
h1: Histamine here causes itching, swelling and hives in allergy.
h2: Histamine here tells the stomach to make acid.
gaba: A chloride channel that calms neurons when GABA binds.
pp: The final pump that pushes acid into the stomach.
cox: Makes prostaglandins (pain, fever, inflammation) and thromboxane (platelet clumping).
ace: Turns angiotensin I into angiotensin II, which squeezes vessels.
at1: Angiotensin II here squeezes vessels and keeps salt.
ins: A tyrosine kinase that lets cells take in glucose.
sert: Recycles serotonin back into the neuron, ending its signal.
nkcc: Pulls salt back into the body from urine.
hmg: The rate-limiting enzyme for making cholesterol.
vkor: Recycles vitamin K so clotting factors can be activated.
nmda: A glutamate channel key for learning; overactivation damages neurons.
naka: Pumps sodium out and potassium in.
ca: Lets calcium in to trigger contraction.
na: Opens to fire an action potential.

drugs: Relaxes airway muscle → airways open in an asthma attack.
Blocks adrenaline at the heart → slower, gentler heartbeat.
Blocks β1 (and β2) → slower heart; can tighten airways, so careful in asthma.
Squeezes blood vessels → raises blood pressure; also unblocks a stuffy nose.
Relaxes blood vessels → lowers blood pressure.
Turns down sympathetic outflow → lower blood pressure and heart rate.
Blocks acetylcholine at the heart → faster heart rate; dries secretions; dilates pupils.
Constricts the pupil and opens drainage in glaucoma.
Blocks acetylcholine at muscle → paralysis for surgery (patient on a ventilator).
More acetylcholine stays at the junction → stronger muscles in myasthenia gravis.
Activates μ receptors → strong pain relief; slows breathing, so it's closely monitored.
Blocks D2 → reduces hallucinations; can cause stiffness (blocks movement dopamine).
Blocks serotonin's vomiting signal → less nausea after chemo or surgery.
Narrows head vessels and calms trigeminal pain → stops a migraine attack.
Blocks histamine → less itching, sneezing and hives (barely sleepy).
Blocks histamine at the stomach → less acid.
Makes GABA open the chloride channel more often → calms neurons, stops seizures.
Switches off the acid pump itself → strongest acid reduction (ulcers, reflux).
Irreversibly blocks COX → less thromboxane, so platelets clump less (heart attack prevention).
Reversibly blocks COX → less prostaglandin, so less pain, fever and inflammation.
Less angiotensin II → vessels relax, lower blood pressure; protects kidneys in diabetes.
Blocks angiotensin II at its receptor → lower blood pressure, no ACE cough.
Activates the receptor → GLUT4 moves to the surface, glucose enters cells.
Blocks serotonin recycling → more serotonin in the synapse over weeks.
Blocks salt reabsorption → lots of urine, removes fluid in heart failure.
Liver makes less cholesterol and pulls more LDL from the blood.
Fewer working clotting factors (II, VII, IX, X) → blood clots less.
Dampens excess glutamate activity → used in Alzheimer's disease.
More sodium in heart cells → more calcium → stronger squeeze; slows AV node.
Less calcium into vessel muscle → vessels relax, lower blood pressure.
Blocks sodium channels in nerves → no pain signal from that area.
Less uric acid made → prevents gout attacks.
